# Part VIII. Communication and Connection {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes before negotiation

Language is not a file transfer. Words are evidence from which another person infers meaning, intention, emotion, and relationship. Communication therefore belongs before negotiation: readers first need the tools for partner-centered attention, responsive questions, visible listening, and repair before applying them under bargaining pressure.
:::

## Guiding questions

- Which level of conversation is each person trying to have?
- What am I guessing that I could ask?
- How can understanding become observable?
- How can honesty remain warm enough to be usable?

## Bridge to the next part

Communication makes hidden meanings more recoverable. Part IX adds strategic interdependence, alternatives, interests, information, and power: understanding now has to support an agreement that each side can accept and implement.
